subject: Heraldic hatching
hook: HERALDIC HATCHING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Engravers invented a standardized visual code of lines and dots so black-and-white prints could convey full heraldic colors.
title: Why Old Shields Are Covered in Secret Dots and Lines
description: Before color printing existed, artists needed a way to display family crests accurately in monochrome. Here is how engravers encoded full heraldic colors into tiny engraved patterns.
narration: HERALDIC HATCHING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture decorative shading drawn across an antique coat of arms. But those fine scratches were never intended to show shadow. They were a precise method of painting without paint. Seventeenth-century copperplate printmakers could not affordably reproduce tinctures. So craftsmen devised an exact visual cipher. Distinct patterns of horizontal bars, vertical dashes, and speckles told readers whether a shield was red, azure, or gold. Every patterned line was secretly broadcasting a specific brilliant hue.
